chieftain.banner: The Ogre Chieftain blocks your path!
challenge: The Ogre Chieftain hauls itself off the bier at the barrow's bottom.
There will be no fleeing from this one. Stand and fight?
chieftain.name: Ogre Chieftain
victory: The chieftain falls, and the barrow goes very quiet.
Beneath the bier, something answers. A seam of light opens in the floor.
The stone had a ward carved into it. It is cracked now.

drowned.banner: The Drowned Warden rises from the ward!
challenge: The water above the ward turns over, and something stands up out of it.
It has been cutting the other side of these letters for four hundred years.
There is nowhere to run to down here. Stand and fight?
drowned.name: Drowned Warden
victory: The Warden comes apart, and the cutting stops.
For the first time in eleven years the ward is quiet.
Above you, very faintly, the lamps of Hollowmere go out one by one.

barrow1:33,6.text: A heavy iron key, green with age.

lines: The Chieftain was not the barrow's tenant.
He was its warden. Somebody set him on
that bier and told him to sit, and he sat
for four hundred years.
Lyra read the letters before the floor
split. Forty, cut in fours. Half a sentence,
she says. And a name at the end of it,
the way you sign a letter: VAIL.
Cold comes up through the crack in the ward.
Not the cold of a cellar. The cold of
somewhere with no season. The letters were
a sentence, Lyra says. Nobody read it.
You walk back into Rivenbrook at dawn.
Every lamp on the wall is lit. Your runner
did that. Halvard meets you at the well
and does not ask what you saw.
You walk back into Rivenbrook at dawn.
There is frost on the south end of town.
In spring. Halvard meets you at the well
and does not ask what you saw.
The other half of that sentence is cut
under ice, four hundred miles north, in a
town that lights its lamps at noon.
Its keeper went down eleven years ago.

and who has been cutting the other half
one.hook: Your journal is saved. Somebody up north is still cutting.
one.subtitle: THE WARDEN OF THE BARROW
one.title: CHAPTER ONE

lines: The ward under the mere is one half
of a sentence. The other half was cut
under a barrow four hundred miles south,
and you broke that one in the spring.
Kestrel Vail climbs the keepers' stair
for the first time in eleven years.
She does not say a great deal. She holds
her daughter's hand the whole way up.
You come up into Hollowmere at noon,
and Hollowmere is dark. Every lantern.
"They never burned to keep it out,"
Kestrel says. "They burned to keep it asleep."
The mere is open water. In midwinter.
Steaming. Whatever slept under two halves
of one sentence has had both halves
taken from it in a single year.
South, the Mere Road goes dark one lamp
at a time. Not all at once. In order, from
the water, at the pace of someone walking.
Bram is out there with a taper.

Chapter Three: WHAT THE LAMPS WERE FOR
and what walks when they go out
two.hook: Something is walking the Mere Road south. Bram is on it.
two.subtitle: THE COLD BELOW
two.title: CHAPTER TWO

chain_mail.desc: Turns a blade. Slows a step.
chain_mail.name: Chain Mail

flame_brand.desc: Its edge burns. Ice hates it.
flame_brand.name: Flame Brand

frost_pike.desc: Cold to carry. Colder to be hit by.
frost_pike.name: Frost Pike

furs.desc: Warm. That is the entire argument.
furs.name: Thick Furs

guard_charm.desc: Someone wanted you to come home.
guard_charm.name: Guard Charm

ice_charm.desc: Cold to hold, and it keeps the cold out.
ice_charm.name: Rime Charm

iron_halberd.desc: Long enough to keep trouble at arm's length.
iron_halberd.name: Iron Halberd

keeper_coat.desc: Waxed against water that is colder than water. Keeps a flame.
keeper_coat.name: Keeper's Coat

knight_plate.desc: A wall you can walk in.
knight_plate.name: Knight Plate

lake_mail.desc: Scales cut from something that lived in the mere.
lake_mail.name: Lake Mail

lamp_key.desc: Her mother's. It still turns the ones on the bridge.
lamp_key.name: Sera's Lamp Key

lantern_stone.desc: Hollowmere keeps its lamps lit with these.
lantern_stone.name: Lantern Stone

mere_wand.desc: Lake-glass, still cold from the water.
mere_wand.name: Mere Wand

moon_rod.desc: Cold to hold. Sharpens a spell.
moon_rod.name: Moon Rod

rimeblade.desc: The edge frosts over as you draw it.
rimeblade.name: Rimeblade

sage_cane.desc: Carried by healers who walk far.
sage_cane.name: Sage Cane

sage_pendant.desc: Holds a little more of the well.
sage_pendant.name: Sage Pendant

silk_robe.desc: Woven to carry a spell cleanly.
silk_robe.name: Silk Robe

swift_boots.desc: The gauge fills that bit faster.
swift_boots.name: Swift Boots

warden_coat.desc: Lined, hooded, and older than anyone wearing it.
warden_coat.name: Warden Coat

warden_staff.desc: Hollowmere work. The head is a seal, not an ornament.
warden_staff.name: Warden Staff

open: The iron gate stands open. The stair falls away below.
shut: An iron gate, barred and locked.
The lock is old, and it is not going to give.

open: The keepers' hatch stands open. Cold comes up out of it.
shut: Planks and iron, set flush into the shore.
There is no handle on this side. It opens for keepers.

open: The west pass. Someone has been keeping the road clear.
shut: A pass west, choked with thorn and rockfall.
Nobody has come through here in a long time.

options: Send a runner back with word
replies: Aldric writes three lines for the boy at the gate and adds a fourth: light the wall.
He does not know why he adds it. His hands wanted to.
Every hour up here is an hour the chisel down there is not answered.

lines: The shrine sign at the mouth of the barrow has been re-cut. This week. The chisel marks are still pale.
Somebody knows this place is open and did not tell Rivenbrook.
Aldric looks back up the road. Halvard said take care. He did not say come back with word.

options: We are not here to read
replies: She reads with her fingers, lips moving, and stops at the last four.
"There is a name," she says. "VAIL. Whoever cut this signed it."
She looks like someone who has read the first half of a letter addressed to her.
"Fine." She steps back. "But once it is broken, nobody will ever know what it said."
She is right. You do it anyway.

lines: Wait. Before anyone touches it. Those are letters, not a pattern.
Forty of them, cut in fours. It is a sentence, {name}. Half of one.
Give me a minute with it. One minute. Then do what you came to do.
barrow2.speaker: Lyra

lines: Hold out your hand. No - the other one. You keep that one free. I have been watching.
It is a lamp key. Every keeper gets one at twelve and loses it by thirty.
That one was hers. It still turns the ones on the bridge, so do not drop it in the mere.
{name}. That is the first time I have said your name without the town in front of it.
hollow.speaker: Sera

lines: You asked me what I promised. Out on the road, before I told you to ask later.
Not to let one go out. That is all it is. Nobody ever said why.
I have added you to it. You do not get a say in that.
Now stop looking at me like that and go and buy a coat.
hollow.speaker: Sera

lines: You never asked me again. Out on the road. What I promised.
Good. Keep it that way until this is finished.
Then ask me, and I will still be here, and I will tell you.
hollow.speaker: Sera

lines: Come down to the shore. Past the lanterns. Right down to the ice.
There is a hatch under that snow with a keeper's lock on it. It has never been opened by anybody who was not one of us.
My mother went through it eleven years ago to re-cut the ward.
The town buried an empty box that winter and told me it was the cold. I was twelve. I believed them for about four years.
You have her key. I gave it to you and I knew exactly what I was doing.
Open it.
hollow.speaker: Sera

lines: Lanterns. The whole length of it. Every one of them lit.
Nobody has been down here in eleven years, {name}.
So somebody has been lighting these.
mere1.speaker: Sera

lines: The room at the bottom of the keepers' stair is not a tomb.
It is a workshop. Stone chips underfoot. A whetstone worn into a saddle.
A tally scratched into the wall in fours, and the fours go on and on and on.
Hold on. Look at the lamps - every one of them lit, all the way back.
Somebody walks this road at dusk to do that. Every night. Alone.
If the road goes dark, Hollowmere goes dark, and then it is just you down there.
So I am staying up here and keeping them lit. No, do not.
{name}. I have followed you into one hole in the ground already.
Let me be useful where you can still find me.
shore.speaker: Bram

lines: He is going to light every one of them, you know. All the way to the bridge.
My mother did that. Not the whole road - ours, and the two either side, because the Marrows are old.
I thought it was a chore. Then she went in the winter, and I went out at dusk anyway.
That was when I understood it was not a chore. It was a promise.
Ask me what I promised. No - ask me later. When we know what is under the water.
shore.speaker: Sera

replies: She does not say anything else for a long while. Neither do you.
The lamps take, one after another, all the way down to the bridge.
"There," she says. "Now I have kept it twice."
She stands, walks on ahead of you, and lights the next one anyway.
She does not sound angry. Somehow that is worse.

lines: Stop a moment. The ice is talking.
It does that when it is thinking about breaking. Grandmother said it was the mere clearing its throat.
We are going down there soon, and one of us is going to say something stupid.
So it may as well be tonight. Sit with me until the lamps take.
shore.speaker: Sera

replies: She sits with him until the frost comes off the inside of the window.
"It is not in him," she says in the morning. "It was visiting. It is looking for something, and he is not it."
"Then I will sit until dawn," she says, "and leave when you do."
She does. You do not ask what she saw.

lines: Pell's boy. Tam. He has been shivering since the night the barrow opened, and he is not ill.
I can sit with him tonight. It costs us the night and I do not think I can help him.
I think I should be there anyway. You decide where we sleep, {name}.
town.speaker: Mira

after: Say the word and I will go first. That is the job.
Have you talked to the lamp girl? She knows something.
lines: {name}. I heard what came out of that barrow, and I heard who went in.
Four hundred miles I have not seen you, and you still walk like a recruit.
They are lighting the lamps at noon here. Noon.
I am not letting you go down there alone twice. Move over.
hollow.name: Bram

after: I keep the lamps because my mother did, and hers.
Nobody ever said why. We just never let one go out.
lines: Careful. The mere took two dogs and a cart this week.
It has not frozen in summer since my grandmother was small.
You are the one from Rivenbrook. You broke the ward.
No - do not apologise. My family cut that ward. We should have told somebody what it was for.
I am coming with you. It is my mess as much as yours now.
hollow.name: Sera

lines: Beds are warm. The mere is not. Fifty gil.
hollow.name: Keeper Ilse

lines: Cold-country work. It weighs more and it is worth it.
hollow.name: Armourer Fenn

lines: Lamps at noon, lad. Lamps at noon.
My father said the day we stop is the day it comes up.
hollow.name: Old Marrow

lines: It came up. My father was right, and I am too old to be pleased about it.
The lamps went out and the water steamed. Then Kestrel Vail walked up the stair.
I skated on the mere once. Once.
Sera pulled me out and did not even shout.
hollow.name: Pip

lines: The mere is not frozen any more. It is steaming. In winter.
Sera said stay off it. I am staying off it. I am not stupid twice.
We watch the water, not the road. The road never hurt anybody.
hollow.name: Watchwoman

lines: We watch the road now.
The lamps on it are going out one at a time, south, at a walking pace. Your big friend is out there.

after: Room is on the house tonight. You have earned the bed.
Do not tell the others, but I have been leaving a lamp lit facing south.
lines: Welcome to the Amber Lantern.
inn.name: Innkeeper Bryn

lines: Potions, ethers, and a bomb or two.
inn.name: Quartermaster

lines: If you press {cancel} you can run! Grown-ups always forget.
inn.name: Nib

after: It is quiet. I had forgotten that was a thing rooms did.
Take my hand, girl. I have not let go of anything in eleven years and I am out of practice.
lines: Do not touch the letters. Whatever else you do down here.
Eleven years. Forty letters. Cut them and it holds, and then the water takes the edges off them again, and you start at the first one.
You are Sera. You are grown.
I know. I know exactly what I did. Say it to me afterwards and I will stand still for it.
The thing on the other side of these is cutting too. It has been cutting the whole time.
Kill it, and I can stop.
mere2.name: Kestrel Vail

lines: Rivenbrook has stood a hundred years, {name}.
Something stirs in the Thornwilds. A chieftain, the scouts say.
And the shrine sign on the south road has been re-cut. Fresh marks, this week. It was not us.
Take the south gate. And take care.
town.name: Elder Halvard

lines: You came back. Sit down, {name}. You look like the barrow looked at you.
Somebody was tending that seal for four hundred years. Somebody who was not us.
And now nobody is.
Your runner reached us before you did. We lit every lamp on the wall.
I do not know why that felt like the right thing to do. It did.
Sit down, {name}. You look like the barrow looked at you.
Kestrel Vail. So that is who was cutting.
I danced with her once, at a harvest, forty years ago. She had cold hands even then.
The wall lamps went out last night, north to south, and came back. I have stopped asking why.
These beds were carrots last spring.
The south row will not take this year. Not carrots, not weeds, not anything.
I put my hand in the soil down there and it is cold as a well. In spring.
town.name: Gardener Pell

lines: The fence held. The frost did not go back.
It has come up to the third row now, and my boy will not go near it. Good.
Green. Look at it. The south row came back the day you say the water went quiet.
I am not asking how. I am planting carrots.
I saw a wolf as big as a cart!
Its breath did not steam. Mum says I made that bit up. I did not.
town.name: Tam

lines: Did you SEE it? Was it bigger than the mill?
I am not allowed past the fence now. Ma says the ground is wrong.
I am cold all the time and I am not even ill.
The healer sat with me all night. She did not sing or anything. She just sat.
She said the cold was not in me. It was visiting. It is looking for something and I am not it.
The lamps on the wall went out last night. All at once. Then they came back on.
Nobody touched them. I was watching. I am always watching.
Beyond the gate is the Thornwilds. Fight or flee, but never dawdle.
Press {menu} any time to open your journal.
town.name: Gate Guard

lines: We heard the barrow from here. Like a door, a long way down.
Then the frost came up the road to the gate. In spring. I have stopped saying "in spring".
The wall lamps went out last night on their own. North to south, one after another.
Then they came back. I have not slept and I am not going to.
The Amber Lantern keeps a bed and a stocked shelf.
Rest before you go. Only a fool walks the wilds tired.
town.name: Gate Guard

lines: Nobody told us anything. We lit the wall lamps when the frost reached the gate.
Seemed the thing to do. Nobody could say why.
Your runner came through at dusk. We had every lamp on the wall lit before dark.
Halvard's orders. I would have done it anyway. My hands wanted to.
A pedlar from the north says the Mere Road lamps are going out. One a night.
Like somebody walking. I keep the wall lit. It is the only thing I know how to do about it.
Steel I can give you. Courage you bring yourself.
Pell's boy keeps bringing me monster teeth. They are river stones. I keep every one.
town.name: Smith Orla

lines: Bring me the chieftain's plate and I will make you something out of it.
Whatever cracked in that barrow, you will want better steel than this.
Four hundred years that ward held, and it was cut with a chisel.
I would like to meet the smith who made the chisel. I would like to know what it was quenched in.
Buying? The inn keeps my stock these days.
Too many bandits on the south road for an honest cart.
town.name: Pedlar Voss

lines: The south road is quieter since you went down there.
Quieter is not the same as safe. The bandits left. Bandits know things.
Carts from the north say the Mere Road lamps are going out. One a night, in order.
Like somebody walking it. Nobody has seen who.

sign_after.barrow1: Carved into the lintel: THE CHIEFTAIN SLEEPS BELOW. Under it, newer: HE IS AWAKE. RUN.
sign_after.wild: THORNWILDS SHRINE - The barrow below is sealed. The letters are fresh cut. Someone re-carved this recently.

sign_text.barrow1: Carved into the lintel: THE CHIEFTAIN SLEEPS BELOW. LET HIM.
sign_text.hollow: HOLLOWMERE - Keep the lanterns lit. Keep off the ice.
sign_text.mere1: Cut over the stair, in the keepers' hand: WE GO DOWN SO IT DOES NOT COME UP.
sign_text.shore: THE MERE ROAD - Do not stop between the lamps.
sign_text.town: RIVENBROOK - The Amber Lantern, rooms and remedies.
sign_text.wild: THORNWILDS SHRINE - The barrow below is sealed. It was sealed for a reason.
